grammar_focus: 综合复习(Review KS36–45)主考——must have done(对过去推测,课文核心)、被动 had been done(KS45)、间接引语 tell/say that(KS39)、be going to(KS36)、将来完成时 will have done(KS37)、虚拟条件(KS40)、as if + 过去完成(KS38)、be able to(KS43)——以本课'嗜酒鬼魂'故事里出现的结构为重点串讲
scene: 伊恩·汤普森先生最近买下的一家小酒馆又要出售了,因为那里闹鬼。他告诉我,有天夜里怎么也睡不着,因为听到酒吧里传来一阵奇怪的响声。第二天早上,他发现门被椅子堵上了,家具也被挪动过;虽然睡前把灯关了,早晨灯却都亮着。他还说发现了5个空威士忌瓶,这肯定是鬼魂头天晚上喝的。当我暗示说一定是村里有人来喝免费酒时,汤普森先生摇了摇头。村里人已经告诉他,即使他把酒馆白送人,他们也不要。

grammar_card.title: 综合复习:对过去推测 must have done + 各时态回顾
grammar_card.intro: 本课把 L36–45 学过的结构串起来复习,重点是'对过去的推测'——用 must have + 过去分词,表示'过去一定发生了某事'。顺带回顾被动(had been done)、间接引语(tell/say that)、be going to、将来完成时、虚拟条件等。全用本课句子举例。

rows: 对过去推测 must have done
The ghost must have drunk the whisky.(一定喝了)
过去完成被动 had been done
The doors had been blocked by chairs.(被堵住)
He told me that he could not sleep.(告诉我)
He is going to sell the pub.(打算卖)
将来完成时 will have done
Workers will have completed the roads.(将已完成)

specialRules.rule: 对过去的推测用 must have + 过去分词:The ghost must have drunk(鬼魂一定喝了)、villagers must have come in(村民一定进来过)。
specialRules.mark: must have done = 过去一定…

specialRules.rule: 过去某次'终于做成'用 was/were able to,不用 could:he was able to sleep again(终于又能睡了)。
specialRules.mark: 成功做成用 was able to

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What evidence is there of a ghost?
options: Strange noises, blocked doors, moved furniture, and empty whisky bottles

passage: A public house which was recently bought by Mr. Ian Thompson is up for sale. Mr. Thompson is going to sell it because it is haunted. He told me that he could not go to sleep one night because he heard a strange noise coming from the bar. The next morning, he found that the doors had been blocked by chairs and the furniture had been moved. Though Mr. Thompson had turned the lights off before he went to bed, they were on in the morning. He also said that he had found five empty whisky bottles which the ghost must have drunk the night before. When I suggested that some villagers must have come in for a free drink, Mr. Thompson shook his head. The villagers have told him that they will not accept the pub even if he gives it away.
